Visual Design.assessment:
# Cycle 46 — Visual Design Reviewer

**REVISE.** The final certificate and its external-link icon now form one focus target in RTL. The pinned headers still lose visible characters during RTL panning in the compiled preview.

## Independent inspection

I tested Google Chrome against port 47855 and compared the rendered result with cycle 45 on port 47854 and the accepted port 47851. Coverage included 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and pure-black dark. I inspected all twelve paired Home and context sheets under `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-46/`. I also captured fresh Home pages with RTL set in the document before initial layout for the baseline and cycles 44, 45 and 46. The four columns show matched start, midpoint and end positions in both themes. [Four-version RTL comparison](rtl-phone.webp).

I tested horizontal panning, single and rapid refresh, forward and reverse keyboard navigation through every credential, phone Explorer, the Blog listing and selected Azure search result, the Linux table, Azure prose and code, the local and global Home graphs and a live motion preference change. Fresh screenshots and measurements are in `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/visual-47855/`.

## Findings

- **Material, RTL masking.** At x=349 of the 390px dark table crop, a solid stroke in the final “o” of “Todo” still falls from #f5f5f5 at the start to #303030 at the middle and end on the black page. In light mode it falls from #141413 to approximately #cdcdcd on #faf9f5. All three right-aligned row headers lose ink within the last 28px. Cycle 45 and cycle 46 have identical samples. This occurred when RTL was set in the initial HTML and when the document direction changed at runtime.
- **Demonstrated cause and maintainability.** The source change in `quartz/styles/custom.scss` uses `:dir(rtl)` to move the mask from the table onto its scrolling link cell. The emitted `index-081a2b1c.css` translates the direction selector into a set of RTL language selectors, including `:lang(ar)` and `:lang(he)`. The English preview has `dir="rtl"` and retains its English language tag, so its entire table gets the mask. The render and asset explain the failure without a stylistic judgment. A direction flag on the existing scroll wrapper can use the same computed direction that determines its overflow; verify the delivered CSS before acceptance.
- **Keyboard improvement.** The scoped `unicode-bidi: isolate` on certificate links keeps each icon with its label. For 120 focus checks covering ten links in each direction, three widths and both LTR and RTL, every center hit the correct link and every full outline fit inside the scrolling wrapper. Cycle 45’s final AZ-900 outline extended beyond the phone viewport by 352px. Cycle 46’s first RTL certificate is now the first certificate in document order. The CAISP and dash values held their positions in both directions after pan and refresh.
- **Graph and responsiveness.** Local and global graphs rendered after entry, ordinary refresh and rapid refresh under desktop Chrome’s default graphics path and with WebGL disabled. Hover-capable wide views maintained the graph’s dedicated palette and margins. Escape returned focus to its launcher. A phone and a reduced-motion initial desktop page had no graph canvas, and changing the desktop preference removed the active canvas. The LTR table retained its last column at 418px, 128px and 97px respectively; no Home viewport showed page-wide horizontal overflow.
- **Theme, typography and surroundings.** The two short status values retained their 14px SN Pro text and label spacing. The Source Serif 4 reading column, TX-02 code at 14.5px/22px, responsive list, search result outline, Explorer and ordinary article table kept their original hierarchy and spacing. The shortened refresh captions now fit the phone comparison sheets. One-pixel sticky-divider variations in earlier phone captures are cosmetic. The remaining required correction is the RTL pinned-header mask.

Responsive and Accessibility.assessment:
# Cycle 46 · Responsive and Accessibility Reviewer

**REVISE.** Bidi isolation fixes the RTL focus failure. The compiled stylesheet still fades all three pinned row headers.

- **Medium defect demonstrated on the published result.** With the original English Home served with `<html lang="en" dir="rtl">`, the midpoint and end positions visibly fade the last letters of “Obtained”, “In Progress” and “Todo” in both themes. The cycle 46 source attempts to apply the fade only to the scrolling link cell. The stylesheet actually served, `index-081a2b1c.css`, substitutes a list of `:lang(...)` selectors for `:dir(rtl)`. Chrome reports RTL computed direction, but the table retains the gradient and the link cell reports `mask-image: none`. The same failure is visible in the cycle’s own RTL phone sheet. Use an explicit direction attribute or the measured table direction for this selector. This is a functional contrast and legibility problem.
- **Keyboard improvement.** I checked all ten actual link text nodes, their external icons and the focus treatment separately across 520 focus stops. The matrix covers forward and reverse traversal, all three widths in both themes and directions, initial RTL scroll fractions 0, 0.5 and 1 and forced-colors samples. Every label and external icon stayed inside the scrollport, and each label’s center hit its focused link. In particular, reverse focus now brings both AZ-900 and its icon into view at 390px. Focused content was unmasked and had a 2px solid outline.
- **Panning, contrast and reflow.** CAISP and the dash remain beside their labels when panned, including JavaScript-disabled pages in each direction at 390, 900 and 1440px. LTR end and midpoint reload values on the live site were 430/215px, 128/64px and 97/49px. Signed RTL values survive ordinary and rapid reload. Firefox’s native zoom at 100%, 200% and 400% yielded 1280, 640 and 320 CSS-pixel viewports with both values visible through all pan positions in both themes. No page-wide horizontal overflow was observed. Status text is 14px SN Pro and has 17.50:1 light and 19.26:1 black contrast. Focused-link outline contrast on the page is 13.00:1 light and 15.61:1 black.
- **Surroundings and transition checks.** Live checks and the 12 baseline/candidate table and context sheets at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 cover Home, the Blog listing, the Linux disk article’s table, Azure article code, Explorer, Search, SPA transitions and Graph. Article text still uses Source Serif 4, code uses TX-02 14.5px, and the phone’s wider Linux table scrolls locally. Explorer/Search dismiss back to their initiating controls. The desktop and tablet graph dialog focuses Close, contains Tab and restores its trigger on Escape. Reduced motion closes an active graph, removes the local/global canvases and moves focus to the site title. Restoring motion yields one local canvas. The phone graph stays absent.
- **Maintenance.** The link isolation is narrowly scoped and effective. The compiled directional selector introduces a dependency on language that HTML direction does not imply. Checking the published asset exposed this discrepancy.

Paired evidence is under `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-46/`, including `rtl-phone.webp`. My independent results and full-resolution crops are under `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/`: `third-access.json`, `47855-access-fullkeys.json`, `47855-access-native-zoom.json`, `47855-access-nojs{,-rtl}.json`, `47855-access-motion.json`, and `47855-access-mask-390-{light,dark}-rtl-plain.png`.

CSS and Quartz V5.assessment:
# Cycle 46 · CSS and Quartz V5 review

**Decision: REVISE.** The link isolation fixes keyboard navigation. The emitted CSS still applies the fade to pinned RTL headings in both themes at every tested width.

## Coverage

Reviewed the cycle 46 SCSS against the frozen cycle 45 source and opened the running build on port 47855 in Google Chrome 158. Inspected all six pairs of table and context sheets in `design-evidence/refresh-repair/cycle-46`, the RTL comparison `rtl-phone.webp`, and additional browser screenshots with the mask enabled/disabled. Completed all combinations of 390, 900 and 1440 CSS pixels, light and pure-black dark, without harness errors. Live checks covered Home, both directions at three pan positions, Tab/Shift+Tab, 125% and 150% scaling, ordinary/double refreshes, Search, Explorer, Blog listing, Linux article table, Azure article code, graph opening/dismissal, repeated initialization and reduced motion.

## Improvements and unchanged behavior

- Isolating each link keeps its bilingual inline fragments together. All 38 forward/reverse keyboard samples across LTR and RTL had visible, hit-testable focus. At 390 px RTL the last link AZ-900 occupied a single fragment from x23–83 and its text was on screen. In cycle 45 its text was at x658 while the icon was at x23. All six phone no-JS status samples also passed.
- Status text stayed beside its pinned header in both directions. The LTR Home mask cleared at its endpoint. A 508.80 px fractional endpoint survived refresh. The generic nine-row article retained its table mask on the overflowing phone, without introducing a cell mask. Its measured/tablet and desktop layouts, the 56 Blog rows, eight current search options, editorial type, pure-black theme and 14.5 px TX-02 code agree with the comparison.
- Both graph controls returned focus, reduced motion removed the canvas and ordinary motion restored exactly one local graph. A fresh interrupted global close/reopen recorded one local and one global instance while open, one local after dismissal, and zero uncaught errors. No graph resource or lifecycle change entered this cycle.
- All changes are in the existing stylesheet. Moving the RTL gradient to the scrolling linked cell is an appropriate scope in the source, sharing its values with generic tables. Resolving direction correctly after Quartz's CSS build is necessary for that rule to take effect. Build and unit tests passed; the full type-check still reported the two recorded baseline module declarations.

## Material defect

The compiled stylesheet converts `:dir(rtl)` into a series of `:lang(...)` selectors. The page is written in English and retains `lang=en` when the UI direction is RTL. In every viewport/theme combination at midpoint/end the table still had a gradient and the linked cell's computed mask was none. Cropping the pinned column in each screenshot found a 28 px-wide band of changed pixels when disabling the mask. The paired RTL sheet confirms the trailing portions of Obtained, In Progress and Todo fade at midpoint/end. Example images from the isolated test are `/tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/mask-47855-390-light-normal.png` and `mask-47855-390-light-disabled.png`. The full computed matrix is `css-mask-matrix-47855.json`.

The existing scroll handler already reads the container's computed direction. Make the appropriate selector match that actual direction after compilation, and repeat the pixel and focus comparisons. No additional critical or material defect found.

designDirector.assessment:
## Cycle 46 · REVISE

All three reviewers voted REVISE. Bidirectional isolation held the visible certificate labels and their icons together during keyboard traversal. The proposed RTL-only mask still failed on the emitted page because the CSS pipeline compiled the direction selector into language selectors while the English document retained lang=en. In the actual production stylesheet the whole table continued to fade the pinned column. This is a material reading defect in both themes. Move the Home fade into its scrolling credential cell in a way that survives compilation; exercise ordinary tables as well as the Home focus, label and cue paint.

The first three production builds and their 167-test suites passed. From cycle 45 the full checker returned to the two existing micromorph and remark-parse/lib module declaration failures. No production publication was part of this review. Browser comparisons, including natural rendering with WebGL disabled, were run against frozen preview ports. My independent images and geometry are in /tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/director-browser. Sealed reviewer files are in /tmp/quartz-refresh-repair/{first,final,third}-{visual,access,css}-review.md. Matched screenshots are in design-evidence/refresh-repair/{first,final,cycle-46}.
